title: PS1: bounded all-modulus DCP recovery with polynomial classical and quantum space

claims.statement: For every integer N>=2 and every fixed s in Z/NZ, let n=ceil(log2 N) be the ORIGINAL input bit length. PS1 is the single complete program of proof.md Sections 1-11 with clog(x)=ceil(log2 x) computed by the bit length of x-1 and all logarithms base two. Its fixed global configuration is h=clog(n+2), b=ceil(sqrt((n+1)h)), d=ceil(n/(b+1)), q=512(d+2)h, r_max=b+q, A_retry=2^40(n+2)^12, F_root=2^20(n+2)^8*2^(4(d+2)), R=16 F_root[A_retry(r_max+1)]^(d+2), C_coin=clog(256R), M_src=8192 clog(1024R(n+3)), and M_phase=8192 clog(1024(n+2)). Local stage and modulus parameters are the fixed greedy schedules and exact case distinctions specified there. Using only fresh independent original coset states, PS1 recovers the entire s with unconditional probability at least 251/256>2/3. Total sequential work is T(N,s)=O(B_T(n)), where the full envelope is B_T(n)=(n+2)^12 R 2^r_max with R and r_max exactly as defined above. This includes classical integer/rational arithmetic, memory addressing, circuit generation, all original source copies, quantum gates, measurements, initialization/reset and every failed attempt. The exact growth index of this envelope is 1/2. All constants are absolute, independent of N, s and outcomes. These bounds hold jointly for this same algorithm and parameter choice on every execution branch, including aborts, failed attempts and original source input registers, under rules.md's fully charged classical bit-work and Clifford+T model.
